original_question: What is the largest possible genus of a bar k-visibility graph?
target_in_paper: Section 3.3 (Bar Visibility Graphs), Open Problem 26: determine the maximum graph-theoretic genus attainable by a bar k-visibility graph; the same section immediately beforehand defines bar k-visibility graphs via disjoint horizontal bars and vertical sight-lines intersecting at most k other bars. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))
correct_elements: Your draft identifies the correct graph class (bar k-visibility graphs) and the correct extremal invariant (genus), and it is already a very close paraphrase of the paper’s Open Problem 26. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))
missing_details: It does not define a bar k-visibility graph: vertices are represented by pairwise disjoint horizontal bars, and two vertices are adjacent exactly when there exists a vertical segment joining the corresponding bars that intersects at most k other bars. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))
It does not state that k is the fixed parameter of the graph class; the section treats bar k-visibility graphs for general k. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))

It does not define genus in the paper’s sense: the minimum integer g such that the graph can be embedded on a surface of genus g. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=9f88e968f29258f3f50459952ccc4e41b40a1988&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))

It leaves implicit the scope of the extremum: Open Problem 26 is posed for the class of bar k-visibility graphs itself, with no added n-vertex qualifier in the paper’s statement. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=9f88e968f29258f3f50459952ccc4e41b40a1988&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))
refined_question: For a fixed nonnegative integer k, what is the largest possible graph-theoretic genus of a bar k-visibility graph, where a bar k-visibility graph is a graph that admits a representation by pairwise disjoint horizontal bars in the plane such that two vertices are adjacent exactly when some vertical segment joining the corresponding bars intersects at most k other bars? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))
justification: Open Problem 26 is the nearest official formulation matching your draft, and there is no more precise equivalent reformulation given nearby in Section 3.3. The paper-faithful sharpening is therefore just to unpack the local definitions of bar k-visibility graph and genus, while keeping the scope exactly at the genus extremal question for bar k-visibility graphs and not drifting to thickness, crossing number, rectangle visibility graphs, or other neighboring problems. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))
